title: EDGE: Dare Eig disagrees with eig(A-BK) 1e-4 with unit-circle pair and Q~1e-12
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). May be fuzz trace-check tolerance (no sep term) rather than solver.

[w13 #47 riccati/review] Dare: Eig disagrees with eig(A−BK) by 3.5e-4 and 8.8e-4 when A has an eigenvalue pair exactly on the unit circle (c2d of ±i) plus a repeated unstable eigenvalue and Q≈1e-12. Repro: FuzzRiccati corpus bytes kind 0x9b vals [376 -63 11 -2 0 0 0 -79 -48 -10 0.37 0 100 50 -20 -10], and kind 0x93 vals [0 97 0.5 -2 -37 120 0 55 0 -10 0.37 0 1 -10 44 -10]. Fails identically on 443ab26 (trace check, mateq_fuzz_test.go). Base skips both only because its Rcnd triggers the 'ill-conditioned stable subspace' gate. The fuzz trace tolerance does not account for sep, so this may be a defect in the check rather than in the solver. Files: riccati.go, mateq_fuzz_test.go.


Wave 15 reports folded in:

[w15 #18] [Low priority, degenerate edge case] Dare res.Eig is inconsistent with eig(A−BK) on a problem whose closed-loop eigenvalue sits on the unit circle. Repro: FuzzRiccati input kind=0x47 vals=[-70 -2.5 -35 0 0 0 -7 0 0 -10 0.37 -63 -10 -10 -10 -10] (fuzz id 0abb84263b2deb00). Problem: n=2, m=3, A≈I, Q rank 1, D=0, R=1e-3·I. The branch's X agrees with the oracle to 2.6e-9, and the sum of res.Eig differs from trace(A−BK) by 2.7e-4. res.Eig gives λ≈0.99956, while mat.Eigen of A−BK gives 0.99978. Base gave λ=1−5e-13, and the fuzz target skipped the case. The Newton update moved X by about 1e-9 and λ by about 2e-4, but Eig was not made consistent with the returned K. Files: riccati.go verifyRiccati/closedLoopEig.

title: CORE: TunePIDFRD sampled Nyquist count certifies unstable PIDF loops (close 0 dB crossings; strict Schur-Cohn disagrees)
body:
Found in wave 21 (fix/wave21). Found by pid track (DKOLCU remainder). Not reachable from the shipped search yet, but blocks the Kd/Tf re-solve search improvement. Fix in FRD feasibility/stability checks, not the search: treat the count as unknown when the phase of 1+L between consecutive samples cannot be resolved (|1+L| small vs sample spacing). Files: pid_tuning_frd.go pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict/pidTuningFRDNyquist, pid_tuning*.go.

[w21 #11 pid/fix] TunePIDFRD strict sampled Nyquist count returns an unstable discrete PIDF. Repro: TestTunePIDFRDStrictCertifiesStableDesigns case 'derivative pole near −1' (num [-1.3448981227532175], den [1,-1.5811862552962634,0.8405266355392914,-0.2593403802430281], Dt 0.1, data 0.518..17.35 rad/s, 422 points, PIDF, PM 60, IFormula BackwardEuler). Once the search can step Kd/Tf with Kp/Ki re-solved (patch in the last followup), TunePIDFRD returns {IFormula:1 Kp -1.257051414453467 Ki 2.015450480743815 Kd 0.7560127242993466 Tf 0.5910346344538493 Dt 0.1} and, in the fallback variant, {Kp -0.8903266789306609 Ki 1.6807747216159954 Kd 0.45742098332667525 Tf 0.4823884097135857}. pidFRDStrictStable (exact Schur-Cohn) says both are unstable. I did not check whether the count certified them or only warned. The hole is in the FRD feasibility/stability checks, not in the search. Files: pid_tuning*.go (FRD Nyquist count / pidTuningFRDNyquist).

[w21 #15 pid/fix] TunePIDFRD sampled Nyquist count accepts an unstable loop when two 0 dB crossings fall within about one sample spacing. Repro (internal only; neither base nor the shipped search reaches it, and base with CrossoverFrequency 0.1768 returns unattainable): plant num [0.0029356119296049623, 0.008229341811485028], den [1, 0.16531968867170563, 0.059760631262763785, 0.00972338931651889], data pidExactFRD(1e-3, 1e3, 600 points), PIDF PM45. With the gating removed, the search returned {Kp -0.021754, Ki 0.298056, Kd 4.884193, Tf 0.171156}, which pidTuningFRDNyquist certified as stable. Evidence: a dense sweep finds crossings at 0.1767, 0.2387 and 0.2455 rad/s (margins 46.0°, 46.4°, 306.6°); arg(1+L) winds -270° instead of +90°; the closed loop has a root at Re +0.0024. The 0.2387/0.2455 crossings are 2.8% apart against 2.3% sample spacing. Files: pid_tuning_frd.go pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict/pidTuningFRDNyquist. Suggested fix direction: treat the count as unknown when the phase of 1+L between consecutive samples jumps by more than it can resolve, for example when |1+L| is small relative to the sample spacing.

## Wave 22 follow-ups (folded)
N4MOKA residuals after fix/pid-wave22 83ce3a4 (arc within 1/4 of 0): strict count still certifies unstable PIDFs when a whole resonance loop falls between samples ~10-15% apart while |1+L| stays 0.6-0.8 (repros A, B, the 53.08 resonance plant, and the PIDF on the 4th-order -6.007/-9.631 plant: arg G jumps 64.1 -> -98.2 deg between 2.154 and 2.477 rad/s). Both 3-point fits must agree today; suggested direction: count unknown when arg G changes > ~90 deg between consecutive samples (a 2x neighbour-step ratio missed A at 1.95). Also: pidTuningFRDDesign finish() (~line 146) returns a loose-pass design the strict verdict already knows is unstable when top=false (derivative pole near -1 data); fail on known-unstable regardless of top. Blocks extending the polish to FRD. Files: pid_tuning_frd.go pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict, pidTuningFRDArcHidesZero, pidTuningFRDDesign.

[w22 #28 pid/fix] CORE: TunePIDFRD strict Nyquist count certifies an unstable PIDF across a resonance the samples do not resolve; N4MOKA's arc test does not fire. Plant num [-6.006874817954687, -9.631465973111077], den [1, 0.6088284763961694, 5.978223314083145, 3.2080336945155454, 1.8717858124577227], continuous, pidFRDStrictData over 1e-3..1e3 with 100 points plus a DC sample. For PIDF {Kp -0.04015450361054589, Ki -0.07844207386734459, Kd -0.005065080923915894, Tf 0.3695158773619382}, pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict gives (true, true, true). The companion roots have max Re +0.0031, the exact winding of 1+L is -270 deg, and a dense sweep finds a 6.0 deg crossing. arg G jumps from 64.1 to -98.2 deg between the samples at 2.154 and 2.477 rad/s (14.9% spacing, under the 1.2 threshold for the sparse warning). The circles through the neighbouring samples are small, so the chord/arc test misses it. Suggested direction: treat the count as unknown when arg G changes by more than about 90 deg between consecutive samples. File: pid_tuning_frd.go pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict. The shipped search does not reach it, but this hole blocks extending the polish to FRD.

[w22 #29 pid/fix] N4MOKA residual A (existed before this fix, not fixed): the strict count certifies an unstable PIDF when a whole resonance loop around 0 falls between two samples about 10% apart, even though min|1+L| stays at 0.63, so this fix's margin does not catch it. Repro: TunePIDFRD(PidtunePIDF, CrossoverFrequency 0.9101415155439248) on num [0.07240994924086397 0.059495186577374334], den [1 0.06618095732149026 1.1605932139252835 0.06953950210523521]. Data: pidFRDStrictData continuous, 96 log points on [0.0013095419860959085, 9.526043738954273], exact DC sample prepended. It returns certified {Kp 0.04993265431173388, Ki 8.824601906317316, Kd 6.996393449841795, Tf 0.05481601240176187}. Oracle: companion max Re +0.0295, dense min|1+L| 0.634. Cause: on step [1.0076, 1.1065], 1+L goes from 0.532-1.048i to 0.526+0.657i. The forward fit puts 0 in the lens, but the back fit (sample 0.9176, off the resonance circle) puts 0 0.40 outside its circle, and the count needs both. Base gives the same design. File: pid_tuning_frd.go, pidTuningFRDNyquistVerdict and pidTuningFRDArcHidesZero.

title: EDGE: HinfSyn/Mixsyn fragile controller (pole -1e13); CLPoles disagree with eig(CL.A)
body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #9 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] HinfSyn/Mixsyn can return a numerically fragile controller (a pole at -1e13, gains about 1e12) whose exact interconnection with the plant is unstable [EDGE]. Its reported CLPoles also disagree with eig(CL.A): imaginary parts 1.0008 vs 1.0425. The library's own float CL is exactly stable. Files: hinfsyn.go (central controller build / CLPoles), mixsyn.go. Repro: fuzz tuple kind=0x60 vals=[0 -5 0.5 -2 0 0 0 -100 0 -10 0.37 41 1 -10 -10 -2], then fzDecode, syNormC and syMixWeights, then Mixsyn(G, W1, W2=0.01, nil). G is SISO with poles 0.001+-1i and 3.16 and D=-95. Exactly closing u=-K y on the returned float G and K gives poles 0.0054+-1.037i.

title: EDGE: RootLocus absolute imag/repeat cutoffs (1e-6, 1e-4) treat slow complex poles as real
body:
Found in wave 16 (fix/wave16).

[w16 #45 fuzz/O5FYRC] O5FYRC-2 [EDGE] RootLocus uses absolute cut-offs: imag < 1e-6 in isOnRealAxisSegment and isNearRepeatedReal, 1e-4 for repeated real roots, and 1e-6·max(1,|re|) in computeBreakaway. Slow complex poles are therefore treated as real. Repro: G = w/(s^2+w^2) via A=[0 w;-w 0], B=[0;1], C=[w 0], D=0. With w=1e-7 it reports Breakaway=[0], but the K>0 branches are purely imaginary (+-1.00000005e-7 i), so there is no breakaway. With w=1e-3 it correctly reports none. Two real poles closer than 1e-4 are likewise counted as repeated. File: rlocus.go. The thresholds should be relative to the pole scale.



Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #60] Precision limit, lower priority: in rlocus, a zero or pole cluster at the origin in a system whose other roots are much larger than 1 is not merged. cutoffFloor caps at 1 while the rounding split scales with the realization norm. Repro: companion -1024·s^3(s-512)/((s+3072)^3(s-1024)^2). Zeros at 0 split by about 3.7e-3, and Breakaway lists ±5.86e-6 instead of 0 (oracle [-3072, 0, 1024]). Pre-existing on base and branch. File: rlocus.go (cutoffFloor, nearRealCount floor).

[w17 #63] Pre-existing (base 79a3737 and branch): a real pole of multiplicity 3 or more under positive gain is not reported as a breakaway, although double poles are. Repro: G=1/(s+1)^3, i.e. A=[0 1 0;0 0 1;-1 -3 -3], B=[0;0;1], C=[1 0 0], D=0: RootLocus Breakaway=[] on base and branch. 1/(s+0.5)^3 also gives []. 1/(s+1)^2 gives [-1]. 1/(s+1)^4 gives -0.99999 on base and branch. Cause: eps^(1/m) eigenvalue splitting (imag ≈ 3e-6 for m=3 at |p|=0.5) exceeds the 1e-6·max(floor,|s|) window in nearRealCount and isNearlyReal (rlocus.go; base isNearRepeatedReal has the same issue). This is the same root cause as the LP755Y incomplete item above.


Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #66] Regression from PAOH7X/LP755Y: the breakaway at a multiple pole at the origin is lost for pure integrator chains (k/s^2) when the realization is not triangular. cutoffFloors only treats a pole set as unscaled when every pole is exactly 0. When rounding splits the double pole at 0 (to ±1.6e-16i or ±3.5e-9), the floor becomes that split, so both the nearRealCount repeat window and the cluster test shrink to about 1e-22 and miss it. The real-axis parity rule then decides by chance, depending on which way the split goes and on the gain sign. Base used an absolute 1e-4 window and gave [0], which is correct and robust at unit scale. The branch's own computeBreakaway doc says a net multiple pole is a breakaway, and the exact oracle agrees: q = -N·D' = -2k·s, so s=0 is a double pole with K=0. The same cause makes rotated 1/s^3 return [] (want [0]); base was also wrong there (spurious -8.4e7 only), so that one is not a regression. Suggested fix: treat poles or zeros whose modulus is at rounding level of ||A|| (for example <= sqrt(eps)·||A|| for a double root, eps^(1/k) for multiplicity k) as an origin cluster, rather than testing x != 0.
Branch fix/rlocus-wave17 9144beb vs base 79a3737, run with RootLocus(sys, {0,0.5,2,10}).
(1) A=[[1,1],[-1,-1]] (nilpotent), B=[0;1], C=[1,0], D=0, so G=1/s^2 (positive gain, the textbook double integrator). Poles come back as -2.2e-17±1.57e-16i. Base Breakaway=[0]; branch Breakaway=[]. Debug: fp=fz=1.586e-16, the root of q is exactly 0, and nearRealCount finds no cluster (tol 3.4e-23 against centroid offset 2.2e-17).
(2) A=Q·[[0,1],[0,0]]·Q^T, B=Q·[0;1], C=[-1,0]·Q^T, where Q is a product of Givens rotations with angle 0.3+0.17(i+2j), so G=-1/s^2. Base [0]; branch [].
(3) Sweep case 611: -2.494/s^2 under a random orthogonal similarity. Poles ±3.53e-9 (real). Base [0]; branch [], with debug fp=3.53e-9, negGain=true, and parity count 1 giving 'off locus'.
Controls: the companion realizations [[0,1],[0,0]] (exact eigenvalues) and rotated 1/(s^2(s+1)) (floor 1) are correct on the branch.


Wave 18 redo (fix/rlocus-wave18 37cb8f4..712cb2e) NOT merged; final review blocking:

Regression, wrong value, from the PAOH7X follow-up 7788958 (realCutoffs.multipleRoot in rlocus.go). Distinct, well-resolved poles inside the eps^(1/m) cluster window are reported as a K=0 multiple-pole breakaway, and a complex stationary point is returned as a real breakaway, listed twice once per conjugate root. The window is clusterRadius(m, scale) = min((1e3*n*eps)^(1/m), 1e-4) * max(|Re r|, min(||A||_1, 1)). For m=3 and n=3 that is about 8.7e-5*scale, and the scale is 1 for any realization with ||A|| >= 1. The same rho also bounds |Im r|. So at unit scale, three poles within about 1e-4 are merged. Any pole set slower than about 1e-4 in a unit-norm realization (a companion form or any rotation) is merged as a whole. This brings back the absolute-cut-off-on-slow-poles class that PAOH7X was meant to remove. Base 376552c was correct (no breakaway) in every case below. The behaviour is the same under GOARCH=amd64.
Main repro, canonical companion form at unit scale: G=1/((s+1)((s+1.00005)^2+2.5e-9)), A=[0 1 0;0 0 1;-1.0001000050000002 -3.000200005000001 -3.0000999999999998], B=[0;0;1], C=[1 0 0], D=0. RootLocus(sys,{0,1}).Breakaway: base [], branch [-1.0000333333, -1.0000333333] (same on amd64). Exact Fraction check on the given float coefficients: N'D-ND' = -D', disc(D') = 4a2^2-12a1 = -2.0000016e-8 < 0, so the stationary points are -1.0000333 +/- 2.357e-5i and there is no real breakaway. eig resolves the poles to about 1.4e-7 while they are 5e-5 apart. Merging them would need a coefficient change of about (5e-5)^3, roughly 560 eps, so this is above rounding. The same mechanism shows in a seeded 4000-case base-vs-branch sweep. Rotated companions with poles at the 1e-5 scale and eig error 1e-3..3e-2 relative (well-posed against the stationary-point imaginary parts) give base [] and a spurious branch breakaway in sweep cases 169, 280, 1087, 1770, 2576, 2801, 2902, 3094, 3245 and 3467. Example 169: poles -1.296875e-5 and -2.421875e-5 +/- 1.421875e-5i, K=2.671875. The D' roots are -2.047e-5 +/- 7.3e-6i, and the branch returns [-2.0469e-5, -2.0469e-5].


Wave 18 reports folded in:

[w18 #37] rlocus Breakaway drops a double-pole break-away point once poles are about 1e3 in size: isNearRepeatedReal (rlocus.go) uses an absolute 1e-4 tolerance. Repro: 5-state companion with poles 0, -1536r, -2048r(x2), -3072r, zero at -1024r, k=2.2518e15*r^4, r=sc/1024; call RootLocus(sys,nil).Breakaway. For sc=512, sys.Poles() splits the double pole to -1024 +/- 9.5e-5 and Breakaway includes -1024. For sc=1024 the split is +/- 1.9e-4 and Breakaway is [-1677.78, -2773.74], missing the oracle's -2048. The tolerance should be relative, e.g. about sqrt(eps)*|s|-scaled. Files: rlocus.go (isNearRepeatedReal, computeBreakaway). Unfixed; other track.

[w18 #38] rlocus Breakaway drops a double-pole break-away point at moderate scale because of absolute tolerances. Repro: the WGMRIE plant 2.2e12(s+1024)/(s(s+1536)(s+2048)^2(s+3072)) in companion form. On fix/tf-wave18 the TF is now correct, but RootLocus(sys,nil).Breakaway = [-1677.78, -2773.74], missing -2048. The same loop scaled by 1/16 gives [-104.86, -128.00, -173.36], which includes the double pole. sys.Poles() returns -2048.00019 and -2047.99981 (split 1.9e-4 by eigen rounding, about sqrt(eps)*2048). isNearRepeatedReal uses an absolute 1e-4 and isOnRealAxisSegment / the imag filter use absolute 1e-6, so the split pair is not recognised as repeated. File: rlocus.go (computeBreakaway, isNearRepeatedReal, isOnRealAxisSegment). Tolerances should scale with the root magnitude.

This track has blocked three times, each time on a new regression introduced by a refix (cutoffFloors, then multipleRoot). Before any fix commit, add the accumulated blocking findings as pinned regression tests. The fixer must run the base 2000-case sweep as a frozen regression set after every commit, not only the reviewer at the end.

Under the 0-degree rule G<0 holds at |s|>>poles, and isStationary (|G'/G| <= 1e-2*sum 1/|s-p|) accepts any far point. Base gave [] in these cases.

The branch gives only [-0.16408920] (arm64). The same TF scaled x32 (also exact) fails on amd64 too: branch [-5.25085], base [-5.25, -5.25085]. - BLOCKING: A multiple pole breakaway is reported twice: once at the eig cluster centre and once again as a root of N'D-ND' that multipleRootNear accepts outside the cluster radius. The radius is max(10*spread, sqrt(u)*sigma), and sigma collapses to the pole modulus.
  Evidence: (a) G=1/s^2 as A=[0.5 1; -0.25 -0.5], B=[0;1], C=[1 0], D=0 (nilpotent, not triangular). Branch [-5.67e-18, 0], base [0] (arm64). The same holds for A=[a 1; -a^2 -a] with a = -0.5, 0.25, 2, 0.125 and k = +-1, 36, 0.0054. eig returns an exactly equal pair -5.67e-18, so the cluster radius is 1.7e-25 and the q root at exactly 0 is added again. The pin TestRootLocus_DoubleIntegratorRotated does not check for duplicates. (b) D=1.5, observable companion, num=[1.5 42 424.875 2075.625 6393.75 -4182022.75 10496072.5], den=[1 28 283.25 1383.75 4262.5 8187.5 6875] (double pole at -2.5). Branch [-2.5, -2.5000387, 3.82455, -10.54497], base [-2.5000387, 3.82455, -10.54497]. Exact oracle: [-2.5, 3.8245, -10.545]. Files: rlocus.go computeBreakaway (cluster suppression radius), multipleRoots radius.
- BLOCKING: True breakaways of slow loops are dropped under a non-orthogonal similarity. lp.eval computes G'(s) through an unbalanced dense solve of (sI-A), which is wildly inaccurate here: computed dg/g = 3.5e4 while the exact G'/G is about -1.9e-6. isStationary then rejects real stationary points. Poles are accurate (eig error 1e-12..1e-14) and base was correct. Both arches are affected.
  Evidence: Intended G = -(1/16384)(s-8.106e-6)(s+2.4796e-5)((s+2.5749e-5)^2+2.718e-5^2)/den. num=[-1/16384, -143/2^35, -9061/2^56, -120303/2^77, 1362465/2^96], den=[1, 49179/2^29, 2345031/2^49, 136879713/2^70, 134782623/2^86, 13177079595/2^110]. The observable companion is transformed by A'=T A T^-1 with T unit upper triangular, superdiagonal values cycling (-0.75, 1.5, -2, 0.25, 3, -0.5, 1, -1, 0.5, 2). Exact float-TF oracle: [-2.5774e-5, -2.3517e-5, -2.0727e-5, 3.2823e-5]. Base returns all 4. The branch misses -2.3517e-5 on arm64, and on amd64 it misses -2.0727e-5 and -2.3517e-5. Canonical companions of the same TFs at scales 2^0..2^20 are correct, so the defect is in the realization-dependent eval. Files: rlocus.go eval and isStationary (no balancing or accuracy bound on dg).
- INCOMPLETE: PAOH7X w17 #66 (origin multiple pole under a non-triangular realization) is not fully closed. In 600 randomly Givens-rotated companions of k(s+z)/(s^2(s+p)), the branch misses the origin breakaway in 6 cases (base 0/600). In all 6, rotation rounding splits the double pole into a real pair of about +-5e-9. Example: p=1.375, z=0.03125, k=-0.5, poles +-4.63e-9 and -1.375; branch [], base [0]. This is the same geometry as wave-17 #66(3) (sweep 611), which was a blocking regression, and as frozen-sweep case 207, which the branch exempts as a precision limit on componentwise-conditioning grounds. Pure rotated k/s^2 passes 800/800. The coordinator should decide whether the componentwise argument overrides the w17 #66 requirement.

3. n-gate (generous, ~n<=12) is a numerics fallback to the current eig path, documented.

title: Pidtune 100-200ms on zero-DC continuous-delay plants when back-off fails everywhere (owner decision)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

BIAA3G leftover: on stable zero-DC plants with a continuous delay where the back-off fails everywhere, Pidtune still costs about 100 to 200 ms per call (120 gate checks, dominated by golden-section |S| refinement on delay ripple in pidTuningSensitivityPeak and tailPeak), against about 1 ms before #345, which did not back off on these plants. Examples: P -0.71 s/(s^2+7.44 s+36.6) tau 0.664; PD (-0.464 s^2-0.366 s)/(s^3+11.5 s^2+43.6 s+54.3) tau 0.486. Closing the gap needs a sound early stop for the back-off (no candidate found) or a cheaper |S| refinement rule; that is an owner decision.

title: EDGE: AllMargin misses phase crossings of delay-absorbed discrete loops (realCandidates)
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Distinct from S2RNHI singular band; cross-ref YIWBXS (continuous lightly damped misses).

[w13 #9 margins/S2RNHI] AllMargin misses phase crossings after discrete delays are absorbed (margin.go realCandidates/boundaryRoots). Repro: num [1.1974308853542987e-16], den [1 -6.184746550403649 16.242438259051475 -23.437999081676736 20.022569140290482 -10.09289718715969 2.766371287397997 -0.31573586749987936], dt 0.01, SetInputDelay([]float64{3}). AllMargin gives PhaseCrossFreqs [0.1801 267.8]. A big-float oracle also has crossings at 14.73, 87.71 and 175.93 rad/s, with GM 218, 307 and 341 dB. realCandidates on the absorbed loop returns [0.1795 1.234 13.248 279.16], so two candidates are more than 10% off and two are missing. The double solve evaluates those frequencies correctly (L(14.73) = -1.2437513636616553e-11 + 3.98e-15i, matching the oracle). Margin itself is correct, since the missed crossings have larger GMs.

[w13 #17 margins/review0] AllMargin/Margin miss a phase crossover beside a cluster near z=1 with a 3-sample delay, even where at() resolves (a different mechanism from S2RNHI's singular band). Repro: dt=0.01, num [1.391607534896511e-15], den [1 -5.996928959245808 14.984645931608547 -19.969294133971424 14.969296404721078 -5.984649337733024 0.9969300946206339], SetInputDelay([3]). At w=2.25925, FreqResponse is real negative at -1.0409e-05, and its imaginary part changes sign across w(1±2%) (-6.4e-8i to +4.9e-8i). The crossing survives 20/20 one-ulp coefficient perturbations, and at(w) returns the same value with no error. AllMargin PhaseCrossFreqs is [104.76 314.16] and Margin GM is 297.14 dB, against the true minimum crossing of 99.65 dB at w=2.259. Second repro: num [8.41798900940185e-14], 9-pole den [1 -8.99977808507088 35.99822556730129 -83.99379258894939 125.98759138433863 -125.9844969880358 83.9876037961689 -35.993805000779744 8.998230886657213 -0.9997789716302142], delay 3; it misses w=20.958 (|L|=1.10e-7), and Margin reports 261.5 dB. Files: margin.go rationalLoop.phaseCrossings, realCandidates (pencil candidates of the absorbed z^-d loop). Same on 690c75a.


Wave 14 reports folded in:

[w14 #33] Low priority, extreme |L|. Title: AllMargin misses mid/high-ω phase crossings of a pole ring near z=1 with a 2-sample input delay. Repro: dt=0.01, num [4.415434721389033e-14], den [1 -8.036803991456532 28.258220548727593 -56.77644492436822 71.29705612326164 -57.30004652305295 28.781827662944814 -8.261210980106032 1.0374020840497447], SetInputDelay([2]). title: Pidtune ~6-8x slower on simple auto calls since AUOTFB first-design gate (owner decision on gate grid)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #60] CORE (perf): MaxEvaluations does not bound TunePID runtime on delayed lightly damped plants. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x80, [0,3,0.3,4,0,0,6,0,-1,-3,0.8,-3.5,-10,52,-10,-10]) gives modes ζ=0.1 at 1 rad/s and ζ=0.01 at 2 rad/s, with a 19.95 s output delay. TunePID(PIDF, MaxEvaluations:512) takes 51 s and returns Unattainable. With damp=5 (ζ=1e-3) it takes 169 s. With a 3.16 s delay it takes 0.3 s. Pidtune on the same plant takes 4 ms and returns a design. Related: Pidtune takes about 50 s on fzDecode(0x80, [6,11,0.3,0.5,0,0,6,-7,-0.5,-30,0.2,0.5,38,-100,-10,-10]) (a ζ=1e-5 mode at 1e4 rad/s, 20 s input delay). The likely cost is the Nyquist screen (pidTuningDelayStability). The fuzz bodies skip these inputs (fzPidSystem and fzPidTuneSlow).


Wave 14 reports folded in:

[w14 #13] Perf (owner deferred; not measured): for discrete plants with large external delays and an ideal-derivative candidate (Kd != 0, Tf = 0), the screen now runs float Poly.Roots on a characteristic of degree n+lag+2 for each candidate. Before, the collapsed TF made this about degree 2, and wrong. Lag can reach MaxAbsorbedDelayStates = 10000; the exact retest is capped at n+lag <= 64 but the float path is not. File: pid_tuning.go pidTuningIdealStable.

[w14 #15] Perf (owner deferred): the |S| bound on undelayed TunePID is slow when the first design breaks it. IP3XIC k=10 PD (dt 0.01, num 10x{2.762e-16, 2.633e-16, 6.197e-17}, IP3XIC den) goes from 52 ms to 5.7 s, and nearunit PD from about 3 s to about 12 s. The time is in the bounded re-search plus the bounded floor search (pidTuningSensitivityPeak at a 1% grid step on every candidate). Unchanged designs pay up to about 1.9x (continuous PID 2.8 to 5.4 ms, from the Markov-tail extension of the single |S| check). Files: pid_tuning.go (tuneAt pidSCheck, pidTuningSensitivityPeak). There is no TunePID benchmark in benchmark_hotspots_test.go; adding one would let scripts/benchcmp track this.


Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #33] Optional perf follow-up (owner deferred perf): factorize once with mat.EigenBoth in pidTuningIdealRealizationFloat instead of an eigenvalue-only pass followed by EigenBoth. This would recover most of the +27–47% screen cost at n>16.


Wave 18 reports folded in:

[w18 #14] Perf (owner deferred): TunePIDFRD fallback and back-off paths run 2.1-3.2x base on the bench cases, and sweep evaluations are 4.7x. Failing data spend about two full budgets (strict pass, base pass, two move directions). Possible fix: skip the strict pass when it can provably certify nothing, or share one budget across the move directions.

title: EDGE: Nyquist RHPPoles hides unstable pole ~1.03 beside huge pole (boundary tol ~ sqrt(eps)*max|p|)
body:
Found in wave 14 (fix/wave14). Common root: classifyNyquistBoundary/poleStabilityTolerance scale with spectral radius; sys.Poles() is correct. Stops FuzzFreqResponse within minutes.

[w14 #35 delayfreq/WYLHSA] Pre-existing, numerically extreme, but it stops FuzzFreqResponse within 1-3 minutes: Nyquist RHPPoles is 1 where the fuzz oracle expects 2, for discrete 2-state loops with eig(A) about {1.0018, 5.5e9}. Repro: FuzzFreqResponse inputs kind=0x41 vals=[0.3 -0.25 52 126 58 0 5.5 49 -1 -10 51.37 -15 88 152 74 10] and vals=[0.3 -0.20833333333333334 45 -38 0 0 5.5 0 -1 -80 0.37 0 -50 -10 -10 -10] (dt=0.1); both fail on 0c02feb. Cause: classifyNyquistBoundary puts every pole within sqrt(eps)*max|p| (about 82 here) on the boundary, so it hides a pole 1.8e-3 outside the unit circle. fzNyqPoleClass treats that pole as clearly unstable even though its error band is much wider. Files: nyquist.go classifyNyquistBoundary, nyquist_fuzz_test.go fzNyqPoleClass. Either the library or the fuzz harness needs to change; that call is yours.

[w14 #37 delayfreq/review0] [EDGE, pre-existing on 0c02feb] Nyquist reports RHPPoles=1 for a discrete model with two exactly unstable poles. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[3.950378993621064e+10 3.411907393429129e+10; 3.4119073934291298e+10 2.9468342356123444e+10], B=[0.511703992453149; 0.9647326178866098], C=[-259817.35621375585 997798.2791785806], D=[0], dt=0.7943282347242815), then Nyquist(nil,0). Exact eigenvalues, computed with Fractions: 1.0294509 and 6.897e10, so RHPPoles should be 2. 1-ulp coefficient perturbation moves the small eigenvalue by only ~7e-6. sys.Poles() returns both poles correctly (1.02945, 6.897e10), so the defect is in Nyquist's stability classification: the tolerance appears to scale with the spectral radius, putting 1.029 on the boundary or inside. A second instance: dt=1e-4, eigenvalues 1.0347 and 5.4e12, output delay 20. FuzzFreqResponse hits this in under a minute: kind=0x41 vals=[0.03 -0.8333333333333334 -51 0 0 0 98.5 0 -0.1 -10 -44.9075 -17 -10 -10 -10 -60], failing at nyquist_fuzz_test.go:189 ('intended off-boundary unstable'). Files: nyquist.go (RHPPoles classification), poleStabilityTolerance.

title: CORE: descriptor algebraicPartStatic flags rounding as impulsive on proper index-2/3 chains with modest E singular value (IsProper false, Step/TF ErrImproperModel)
body:
Found in wave 22 (descriptor review). Pre-existing on 2db88fe, unchanged on fix/descriptor-wave22. Not a precision limit: E's small singular value (1e-1..1e-4 relative) is far above the MATLAB rank floor, and the structured oracle response is bounded. The c*N^k*b term exceeds its 1e3*n*eps bound by 1.3-5.3x at stiffRel 1e-1..1e-3 (6.6e4-2e6x at 1e-4 beside index-5/6 chains): the bound does not scale with the nilpotent/b scaling. Files: descriptor.go (algebraicPartStatic, weierstrassReduce nilpotent/b scaling), eigdecomp.go (deflateInfinite).

[w22 #19 descriptor/rev] Title: algebraicPartStatic flags rounding as impulsive: proper index-2/3 descriptor with a modestly small (non-stiff) E singular value returns IsProper=false, and Step/TF return ErrImproperModel (pre-existing on 2db88fe and unchanged on the branch). Repro, in package tests: rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(61, 77)); nf := 1 + rng.IntN(3) (=2); sys, orc, _ := chainDescriptor(t, rng, nf, []int{3}, 0.1, true); sys.IsProper() gives false, nil. The model is proper: the structured oracle orc gives |G(1e6i)| = |G(1e9i)| = 1.4, bounded. Other repros: chains [3] stiffRel 0.01 seed 9; [3] 1e-3 seed 0; [2] 1e-3 seed 35; [2 1] 0.01 seed 7. Failure rate on base over 200 seeds: [3] is 1/200 at stiffRel 0.1, 24/200 at 1e-2, 148/200 at 1e-3, 193/200 at 1e-4; [2] is 4/200 at 1e-3 and 39/200 at 1e-4; [2 1] is 13/200 at 1e-4. Evidence: the c*N^k*b term in algebraicPartStatic is 1.3x-5.3x its bound 1e3*n*eps*max(|c|,cScale)*max(|b|,bScale)*|N|^k at stiffRel 1e-1..1e-3. It reaches 6.6e4-2e6x for stiffRel 1e-4 beside index-5/6 chains. E's small singular value (1e-1..1e-4 relative) is far above the MATLAB rank floor, so this is not a precision limit of the data. Files: descriptor.go (algebraicPartStatic, weierstrassReduce nilpotent/b scaling), eigdecomp.go (deflateInfinite).

## Wave 23 follow-ups (folded)
XSDPXI residuals after fix/descriptor-wave23 (partial). Proper chains beside a small-E pole still read improper: index-3 74/200 (1e-3) and 168/200 (1e-4); index-4/5 condChain 256/310 and 288/301. Mechanisms: (1) weierstrassReduceCore misallocates the stiff mode between D and its residue (error delta_D*s/(s-lambda)); tolerance tuning trades false-improper for oracle failures, residual Sylvester refinement worsens it; needs better-conditioned D/proper part (direct (sE-A) solves at low frequency) or refined infinite deflating subspace (Q/Z vs stiff eigenvector), reduction error ~eps*egap^k. (2) algebraicPartStatic static cut ignores rounding propagated through A (~eps*||A||*||A_inf^-1||): widen only the static decision, not algebraicPolyTerms (widening both broke [5] seed 20 improper). Owner decision (#11): 15 class-4 impulsive seeds (kd<=1e-8, s^1 Markov ~1.6e4*eps relative) now report proper/Step succeeds where base errored; decide whether the XSDPXI/JDKLOX s-term cut treats this as a precision limit (above rounding, so not auto-dropped).

[w23 #14 descriptor/fix] XSDPXI residual (finding 2, still open): proper index-3 chains beside a small-E pole (chainDescriptor(rand.NewPCG(seed,77), 1+IntN(3), [3], 1e-3|1e-4, true)) return IsProper=false in 74/200 and 168/200 cases. weierstrassReduceCore's proper reduction (descriptor.go, confirm/reductionMatches path) misallocates the stiff mode between D and its residue, error δ_D·s/(s−λ): seed 10 at 1e-3 is off by 1.7e-5 at 1e3i and 4.7e-5 at high frequency, with the stiff pole itself accurate to 1e-12. Relaxing reductionMatchTol cuts the false-improper rate but gives proper TFs that fail the 2e-6 oracle check at 1e3i. A residual-based (2,1) Sylvester refinement makes it worse. Needs a better-conditioned way to compute the D/proper part (e.g. from direct (sE−A) solves at low frequency) rather than tolerance tuning.

[w23 #16 descriptor/rev] Title: XSDPXI residual extends to index-4/5. Proper chains beside a small-E pole are read as improper almost every time (pre-existing, slightly improved by the branch). Repro: condChain construction (U,V = Q1*diag(10^(-lc*i/(n-1)))*Q2, Ff/Wf diagonal with Wf[0]=sr, b only on chain heads), chains [4] or [5], sr 1e-2..1e-4, lc 1..3. Repro: rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(10, 77)); nf := 1 + rng.IntN(3); sys, orc, _ := chainDescriptor(t, rng, nf, []int{3}, 1e-3, true). The reduction error grows roughly as eps*egap^k: [3] 1e-4 has 168/200 proper chains still improper, and [4]/[5] at 1e-3 or smaller are mostly improper. The fix needs a more accurate infinite subspace (e.g. iterative refinement of Q/Z against the stiff eigenvector), not a wider tolerance. title: EDGE: scripts/fuzz.sh amd64 replay uses wrong package dir for root-package crashers
body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Tooling bug.

[w12f #21 fuzzsys/U6H6TG] Tooling: scripts/fuzz.sh never replays new crashers from the root package under GOARCH=amd64. For f = ./testdata/fuzz/FuzzX/hash, dir=$(dirname $(dirname $(dirname f))) gives ./testdata, so the replay prints 'FAIL ./testdata [setup failed]'. Seen when replaying the FuzzLFT crasher. The fix is one more dirname level, or deriving the package dir another way. File: scripts/fuzz.sh, replay loop.

title: EDGE: AllMargin misses robust phase crossovers near lightly damped modes; realization-dependent
body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Crossovers robust under rounding (oracle). Cross-ref 42ZG7L, UFBPWZ, VT3OF7 (similar lightly-damped misses) - dedupe on fix.

[w12f #33 fuzzstruct/FUU523] EDGE: AllMargin and Margin miss a phase crossover at a lightly damped low-frequency pair when an exact double integrator and a stiff pole are present. Repro: TransferFunc num=[-4.969549555901367e-05 -136.49013836668794 -6930.639686355759 0.019408431409671963 -2.972934713546136e-06], den=[1 2e6 1.000000000001103e8 0.00859245157249671 0.08427408999794361 0 0], continuous, .StateSpace(). Poles: s^2, a pair at 2.9e-5 rad/s with zeta ~1.3e-6, and -50, -2e6. AllMargin returns PhaseCrossFreqs [] and Margin GM=+Inf. The exact oracle (componentwise-robust) has a phase crossover at w=2.9029824224235686e-05 with GM -190.46 dB; the phase offset is -180/+180 deg at w0*(1-/+1e-6). Same on amd64. Files: margin.go resonanceCrossings/phaseCrossings.

[w12f #35 fuzzstruct/FUU523] EDGE: AllMargin is realization-dependent for a feedthrough-dominated loop with a zeta=1e-7 mode and near-cancelled integrators. Repro: TransferFunc num=[-447.67661499638587 -0.27042549718475767 -4.083782716088854e9 -18.734339369971906 8.388141179041895e-12], den=[1 6.040586492872535e-4 9.12217118175434e6 -1.009712242922581e-5 -2.672975009877894e-18]. The companion realization (.StateSpace()) gives PhaseCrossFreqs [2702.46 3020.2886]. Applying any upper-shear similarity T=I+0.3*triu(ones) or larger gives []. The oracle requires 3020.2886362327736 (GM -53.02 dB; phase offset about 1e-6 deg either side, robust under rounding). Fuzz input: kind 0x84, vals=[-53.083808354550975 13 3.480049108858937 9 0 69 -0.2 -623 -58 19 47.37 98 -16 -10 -3.3333333333333335 -34]. File: margin.go phaseCrossings.

[w12f #44 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, EDGE] AllMargin misses a phase crossover when the loop's realization is badly scaled, although it finds it on an equivalent well-conditioned realization. Repro: FuzzAllMargin kind=0xde vals=[-63 3 59.3 6.625 2 0.07142857142857142 1.4 -57.7 0 16 0.8 66.01 -104 -10 -1.6666666666666667 -60], channel (0,0): n=6, ‖A‖ about 7e5, poles -16966, -0.237±10000j, -0.589 and ~0, C ~ 1e-5, D = -56.6. In the exact rational evaluation the phase offset from -180 goes from +1.19e-6 deg at ω=10000.27 to -7.5e-6 deg at 10000.28. The realization rounding sensitivity there is about 5e-14 rad, so the crossover is robust. AllMargin(sys) returns PhaseCrossFreqs=[]; AllMargin(Ssbal(sys).Sys) also returns []. AllMargin(Canon(sys,CanonModal).Sys) returns [10000.2713, 18761.1] with GM -35.057 dB, matching the oracle. File: margin.go rationalLoop.phaseCrossings / polish / resonanceCrossings.


Wave 18 reports folded in:

[w18 #43] [EDGE] Margin and AllMargin report no phase crossover (GM=+Inf, PM=+Inf) on a D-dominated loop whose exact phase crosses ±180° with |L|=74.5, where GM should be about -37.4 dB. SISO continuous n=6: A rows [-3.621052778337902 -3.1274712544492207 -0.7036583014885595 7163.284872846627 -1848.386251864272 13.572483826745826], [-3.068627991847458 -2.650346852858203 -0.5963087789166936 6186.55146074059 -1596.360702520805 11.719419435425758], [-0.7430135397672757 -0.6417342219340859 -0.1443855357489841 1392.2100564300247 -359.23583426417133 2.6394788364652118], [-7177.720215704098 -6199.333459425002 -1394.8049710175735 -15.450904840151562 1483.7338126427182 28.6681321534807], [1789.8429003980025 1545.8714809299904 347.8098476663391 -1606.2058839073006 -241.8606829237323 112.49988798696154], [13.590458356132176 11.737958667120829 2.6409553874873333 28.54542501926317 112.52102142587427 -53.314511114599604]; b=[-0.9118608758306777 -0.6394617563830491 0.569750334265312 0.9442768504319174 -0.06456443148960145 -0.9788186700204795]ᵀ; c=[5.656293014467941e-07 1.2935760141565169e-06 -1.4020285600901407e-06 -3.8705360231291875e-07 1.6522893429795368e-06 -6.812822097371732e-07]; d=-74.50384797884405. The model has a double integrator and a resonance at 1e4 with ζ≈3e-6. Oracle: Im L changes sign at ω≈9999.999026 (|L|=74.504), and this holds in 6/6 1-ulp perturbations of A. Caveat: the phase stays within 5e-6° of 180° everywhere, so this is a degenerate near-static loop. title: EDGE: Pidtune integrating crossover 3-5x off when z=1 integrator scatters into a cluster
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #60 pidtune/review1] Crossover is still 3-5x off on discrete integrators that rounding scatters into a cluster of conjugate or comparable-distance poles (the integrator is not isolated), outside FI3ZIB's scope. Example from a seeded (z-1)·∏(z-e^(-a·dt)) sweep: nearest pole 2.07e-3 from z=1 with a second pole at the same distance (a conjugate pair); plantCrossoverFreq gives 0.1035 vs 0.0304 for half the slowest pole. Other examples: 0.50 vs 0.163 at ratio 1.22, and 0.245 vs 0.059 at ratio 1.66. These cases have no gain crossover and the same value on base. File: pidtune.go pidtuneIntegratingCrossover / pidtuneSlowestRoot. Designs stay stable.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #10] Pidtune errors in every family when AllMargin's first gain crossing is at rounding level (pidtune.go plantCrossoverSource takes all.GainCrossFreqs[0] as wc). Repro on 690c75a: num [4.905554616319012e-13], den [1 -2.310228431318273 1.8436939371933398 -0.6052316064965124 0.07495077124036684 -0.0032273933261639186 4.2722707242222904e-05], dt 0.1, built with TransferFunc.StateSpace. AllMargin gives a gain crossing at 3.17e-11 rad/s, and P, I, PI, PD, PDF, PID and PIDF all return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable at wc=3.17e-11. Neighbouring plants from the same generator (TestPidtuneRoundedZeroDCIntegrator, PCG(11,3)) whose crossing AllMargin misses get stable designs at wc of about 0.5 times the slowest pole; MATLAB pidtune returns a controller. This is also why sisoEval.at keeps its snapped +Inf (S2RNHI): with that value replaced, 88 of 300 sweep plants flip to errors.

[w13 #64] EDGE: Pidtune and TunePID return ErrInvalidArgument 'no gain crossover, bandwidth or nonzero pole to infer a crossover from' for biproper plants with |G|>1 at all frequencies whose integrator poles sit about 1e-8 off z=1, well above rounding. Repro: discrete Dt=0.1, A=[1.0000000116488188 1.8099675739185816e-08; -7.753540390871093e-09 0.9999999883511813], B=[0.6979798590772273 -0.5033119781891744], C=[1.4839794477710827e-06 -4.772606107217278e-07], D=520.8700127245612, Pidtune(PI, wc=0). The exact integrator takes the integrating path and gets a design. File: pidtune.go (plantCrossoverSource: integratingDCGain and pidtuneIntegratorCluster disagree).

title: EDGE: Mixsyn errors 'gamma not achievable' on numerically singular square static G
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Hidden by FuzzMixsyn gate syNumericallySingularD.

[w13 #44 riccati/IZKUS3] Mixsyn errors on a square, numerically singular static G when the slow-weight pole is not near z=1, continuous or discrete. Repro: G = NewGain(D, dt) with D=[95.76575281793012 30.239088825335227 -40.061662395521715; -128.5980865880245 -71.08545020314747 -2.349984258481528; 153.96097157258234 107.80290777082504 44.625135203013] (σ = 258, 63, 2.7e-13), W1 = ss(0.9048374180359595, 1, 9.468676905422027, 0.5, dt), W2 = 0.01. Mixsyn returns 'γ = 1.4e12 not achievable' for dt = 1, 0.1, 1e-2 and 1e-4, and for the continuous analog W1 = ss(-0.1, 1, 9.95, 0.5). K=0 already achieves γ = max|W1| = 100, so the error is wrong whether or not D is exactly singular. Evidence: hinfGeneralPlant.riccatis accepts γ = 101, 200, 1e3 and 1e5, so bisection succeeds but every controller build or check fails, most likely in the D22 = -D loop shift or wellPosedQ. Base 81b761d fails the same way. The FuzzMixsyn gate syNumericallySingularD hides it. Files: hinfsyn_general.go (synthesize, wellPosedQ, loopShiftIllPosed), hinfsyn.go.

title: EDGE: FRDFeedback m>p absolute pivot tol: false ErrAlgebraicLoop at ||KG||>1e15
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #56 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] FRDFeedback with more plant inputs than outputs solves the m x m system I - sign*K*G with an absolute pivot tolerance (cSolveInPlace). It loses accuracy at a relative error of about eps*||KG|| and returns a false ErrAlgebraicLoop once ||KG|| exceeds about 1e15, although (I+GK)^-1 G is well-conditioned. Repro: G = [[3c+ci, -2c+0.5ci]] (1x2), K = [[0.3],[0.2]], sign = -1. At c=1e14 the relative error is 4e-3; at c=1e15 it is 20%; at c>=1e16 it returns ErrAlgebraicLoop. The exact answer is G/(1+GK), about 4.63-1.71i. Files: frd.go FRDFeedback, frequency.go cSolveInPlace. Fix: solve the smaller p x p I - sign*G*K when p < m, or use a relative pivot test.
